scope: Independent visual-only review of ten baseline candidates; no approvals, model edits, runtime changes, or new execution tests.
evidence: Each ID inspected on comparison board containing actual desktop/mobile closed/open captures plus baseline promotional WebP. Original native screenshots additionally inspected for Argentina desktop-closed, Bangladesh desktop-closed/mobile-closed, and Comoros desktop-closed. Input SHA-256 records are in inspected-inputs.json; boards are derived review aids, not replacement captures.
limits: Still screenshots establish appearance, not temporal shimmer, collision clearance, material configuration errors, or animation correctness.
Boards crop desktop viewer and reduce images; cropped desktop controls are not a UI defect. Native captures remain authoritative.
DPR1 and existing WebGL antialiasing are supplied capture conditions. Supersampling is a conditional renderer experiment, not a proven fix or blanket recommendation.
Promotional lighting, floor shadows, richer microtexture and realism do not themselves establish ordinary finish defects.

findings.observation: Pastel strata and faceted ridge remain consistent across closed desktop/mobile; open interior retains the layered finish. Dark closure seam and abrupt terrain facets also belong to the visible design language.
findings.recommendation: Preserve ridge facets, strata, corner blocks and lid clearance. No definite isolated texture failure is established; do not smooth the terrain or close the dark band to imitate promotional shading.
findings.supersampling: Not specifically justified: triangular color edges are predominantly modeled/stylized terrain, not demonstrated sampling failure.

findings.observation: Native desktop and mobile closed images show pixel-scale breakup in fine ivory textile edges, compressed side motifs and thin diagonal brass/patterned trim. Larger framing and fittings remain readable; open states remain coherent.
findings.recommendation: Trial a modest internal render scale such as 1.5 at DPR1 in an isolated viewer copy, retaining existing AA and every model/material/camera byte or setting. Compare same-size four-state captures, especially front/side motifs and trim. Retain only for visible continuity improvement without erasing intentional weave and with acceptable measured device cost. Otherwise no edit; investigate filtering separately rather than repainting motifs.
findings.supersampling: Targeted experiment justified, efficacy not proven. No motion-shimmer claim. Do not apply globally.

findings.observation: Pale stone courses, stepped temple, green trim and coherent open cavity are visible. Cyan pool reads opaque and simpler than marketing; gold and stone have flatter viewer illumination.
findings.recommendation: Keep still pool, stone grid and stepped geometry unchanged. Water realism and weathering are art-direction differences, not demonstrated shader errors. Only a separately confirmed wrong material assignment would justify a local material correction.
findings.supersampling: No particular sampling defect established; cannot turn the flat-looking pool into realistic water.

findings.observation: Broad soft waves are conspicuous on exterior panels, lid and open underside; native desktop confirms this appearance, not its technical cause. Promotional surfaces read calmer. Volcano, flowers, turquoise band and hardware remain coherent.
findings.recommendation: Do not automatically reduce normals or rebuild panels. Treat broad waviness as stylized stone unless an intended flat-cut-stone brief establishes otherwise. If later scoped, isolate base color/normal/roughness contributions before any material-only correction; no geometry change is justified here.
findings.supersampling: Not appropriate for low-frequency material waves.

findings.observation: Broad stone rippling, ivory closure band, angular basalt and turquoise basin persist across views and occur in the promotional design. Viewer lid appears warmer and brine flatter than marketing.
findings.recommendation: Retain rippled stone, salt rim and rocks. Warm lid tint and flat brine do not prove a color-space or assignment error; do not recolor from differently lit marketing pixels. No bounded defect established.
findings.supersampling: No specific benefit established; material/lighting contrast dominates.

findings.observation: Pale limestone, irregular low reef forms, blue top and dark teal opening rim read consistently on desktop/mobile. Open cavity is complete in the visible views; promotional lighting provides greater depth.
findings.recommendation: Preserve irregular reef relief, pale corner blocks and teal seam. Do not add photographic surface detail or stronger shadows as a purported repair; no localized missing finish or broken seam established.

findings.observation: Strong repeated sediment/wood-like waves appear on body and open interior, with related waviness in marketing. Mangrove roots and tidal channels are coherent; mobile loses fine detail through size.
findings.recommendation: Preserve tidal geometry, roots, teal rim and existing bands. The wood-like versus sediment-bronze reading is a material-style limitation, not evidence of corrupted texture. Do not replace the full material as ordinary polish.
findings.supersampling: Not a remedy for broad repetitive banding; no specific sampling repair established.

findings.observation: Warm flowing wood grain, turquoise islands and mangrove roots retain identity across desktop/mobile. Open underside is wood; exterior landscape is naturally hidden. Promotional grain and foliage are finer.
findings.recommendation: Preserve broad grain, irregular islands, roots and pale feet. Finer marketing wood/foliage is promotional finish disparity, not a localized defect; no repaint or geometry adjustment justified.

findings.observation: Cream limestone, orange cedar lid/interior, green rim and flattened cedar boughs are consistent in actual views. Promotional wood is more muted; tree is hidden by open-lid orientation, not demonstrably missing.
findings.recommendation: Preserve finger-joint-like edges, flattened foliage, rim corner blocks and warm wood. Do not mute the full palette to match studio illumination or treat the hidden ornament as lost geometry.

findings.observation: Bright lake-blue enamel, pale mottled granite, rounded rocks and gold fish ornaments remain coherent across four states. Marketing is more softly lit and grounded; open cavity and underside remain consistent.
findings.recommendation: Retain saturated enamel, pale mottling, irregular granite and dark closure band. No isolated texture failure or material spill demonstrated; do not convert enamel into realistic water or smooth the rocks.
